 Two of the top teams in the RSL, the title-holders against the double Asian champions, face off at Alinma Stadium on Friday
 The Roshn Saudi League returns from the international break on Friday, and does so in style, with Al Ahli hosting Al Nassr is a blockbuster clash that should have major repercussions in the title race.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Can Al Nassr keep pace with Al Hilal at the top of the table , or will Al Ahli revive their title hopes and bounce back from their heavy defeat to Al Shabab last time out?
 So how will the game be won? We examine five key areas that will decide this mouthwatering fixture in Jeddah.
 Al Ahli and Al Nassr are both eying the RSL title this season
 --------
 Crank up the pressure
 This game pits two of the league's most intense pressing teams against each other, which will make for a fascinating tactical battle.
 Both sides are ranked joint-first in the league for possession won in the final third (54), while they are also the top two in the 2026-27 RSL for high turnovers - Al Ahli with 102 and Al Nassr with 95.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Further, no team has had more shots or goals from those turnovers than Al Ahli (20 shots, four goals), while the Jeddah giants and the RSL champions rank in the top two for Passes Per Defensive Action (Al Nassr 8.5, Al Ahli 9.2) and high-intensity pressure in the opposition half (Al Nassr 1,557, Al Ahli 1,409).
 --------
 Ivan Toney vs Bento
 Few have been able to stop Ivan Toney this season, with the England international scoring for fun in the opening months of the season. His 12 goals in nine games place Toney at the top of the RSL scoring charts.
 This week, however, he comes up against one of the best goalkeepers in the league in Bento, who returned to international duty with Brazil in their friendlies these past two weeks in Singapore. On Friday, both players are chasing records of their own.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement For Toney, he could break the mark for the most number of RSL goals scored after 10 games in a season, which is jointly held by Omar Al Somah, Gelmin Rivas, Cristiano Ronaldo and Joao Felix, who all found the net 12 times in 10 matches.
 For Bento, meanwhile, a clean sheet would put him level with Australian Brad Jones for the most clean sheets kept by a foreign goalkeeper for Al Nassr. To that, his record against Al Ahli has been decent, the Brazil international saving 12 of 15 shots on target against him in his previous three club games.
 Ivan Toney is on fire with Al Ahli this season
 --------
 Roger Ibanez vs Joao Felix
 Ever since he arrived at Al Ahli, Ibanez has been one of the standout defenders in the RSL . In fact, since that 2023-24 season, no player has made more interceptions (163) than the Brazilian and, among defenders, only Pedro Rebocho has bettered his 507 possession recoveries.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Still, Ibanez will face a stiff test against Felix, who is starting to show signs of the player that took the league by storm last season.
 While his numbers are down on 12 months ago, Felix still has three goals and seven assists - four of which came in their last game, a 5-3 win against Al Kholood . As such, the reigning SPL Player of the Season tops the 2026-27 RSL assist charts.
 Thus, for Ibanez at least, getting the timing right of when to press up and close the space - and adding to those intercept numbers - will be crucial in shackling Al Nassr's creative fulcrum.
 Reigning SPL Player of Season Joao Felix carries much of Al Nassr's attacking threat
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement --------
 Francisco Trincao vs Al Nassr's left side
 While most of the focus in attack is on Ivan Toney, ignore Trincao at your peril.
 Not only is he a goal threat of his own, with his six this season all coming from open play, but he's also one of Al Ahli's main architects when it comes to chance creation. Only Eduard Spertsyan has created more chances this season (25 to 16), with six of those 16 for Trincao being classified as big chances.
 So the principal focus for whoever plays on the left for Al Nassr, be it Ayman Yahya or Awad Aman, is on nullifying Trincao's impact and limiting his supply for Toney.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement That would deprive Al Ahli of one of their most dangerous weapons.
 New Al Ahli signing Francisco Trincao scoring debut Al Ahli goal
 --------
 Angelo vs Valentin Atangana
 As with any match, the midfield battle will be pivotal, especially for two sides that like to press and pressure as much as these two. In that, those decisive actions to immediately win back the ball are key.
 Looking at the RSL title-holders, Angelo has continued last season's fine form into this: he has five goals already, alongside 18 successful dribbles, highlighting how dangerous he is going forward.
 In contrast, Al Ahli's Atangana is a disruptor, as shown this season by his 32 fouls conceded, 19 tackles and 18 interceptions. However, at Alinma Stadium on Friday, the young Frenchman will need to be wary not to overcommit and give away the ball in dangerous areas.
 Without doubt, whoever gets on top in this area can help control the game for their side.
